title: The Amazing Human Machine 🤖
text: Imagine a robot that can run, jump, taste yummy ice cream, and even give warm hugs! No scientist has ever built a robot this amazing. But guess what? You own one! It's your very own body.

title: What Do You Think?
text: If your body is a super-robot, what are its different parts? Why do we have arms instead of just legs? What would happen if we didn't have eyes or ears? Think about how each part has a special job to do.

content.title: The Parts of Our Body
content.description: Just like a car has wheels, doors, and a steering wheel, our body has different parts that do special jobs. Let's see how they all connect together!

title: Meet Your Body Parts
text: Our body has many parts: Head, Shoulders, Knees, and Toes! We also have five special helpers called Sense Organs. They are the eyes, ears, nose, tongue, and skin. They send messages to our brain about what is happening outside.

content.meaning: The five special parts of our body (eyes, ears, nose, tongue, skin) that help us see, hear, smell, taste, and feel the world around us.

content.title: Oops! A Common Mistake
content.text: Many people think we only feel with our hands. But actually, our skin covers our entire body! This means you can feel things with your arms, legs, back, and even your face!

question: Which body part acts like a camera to help you see the world?

content.title: Reflection Time 🪞
content.text: Close your eyes for one minute. Try to touch your nose with your finger. How did your hand know where your nose is without looking? Teach this magic trick to your younger sibling and ask them how it works!

title: Connecting the Dots
text: Just like animals use their tails for balance or wings to fly, we use our hands to hold things and legs to walk. In the future, you will learn how the brain acts as the remote control for all these parts! It's all connected in the grand web of life.

content.title: Mastery Challenge: The Robot Game 🕹️
content.text: Play a game with your friend! Ask them to be a robot. Give them commands using only body parts. Example: 'Robot, tap your head 3 times!' or 'Robot, touch your knees!' See if they know every single part of their amazing machine.
